 multipath-tools (0.9.4-5ubuntu3) mantic; urgency=medium
 
   * d/initramfs/scripts/{local-bottom,local-top}/multipath: Make initramfs
diff --git a/debian/patches/lp2034471-multipathd-add-Wants-socket.patch b/debian/patches/lp2034471-multipathd-add-Wants-socket.patch
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ef16218
--- /dev/null
+++ b/debian/patches/lp2034471-multipathd-add-Wants-socket.patch
@@ -0,0 +1,27 @@
+Description: Add Wants=multipathd.socket to multipathd.service
+    This solves the issue where systemd knows the start order of the 
+    service/socket, but there is no dependency explicitly mentioned. This 
+    causes an issue if you try to start the socket after the service by doing
+    something such as
+    
+        systemctl stop multipathd.service multipathd.socket
+        systemctl start multipathd.service multipathd.socket
+    
+    The socket would see that it is already active, thus causing an error. This
+    results in the socket ending up in an inactive state.
+Author: Mitchell Dzurick <mitchell.dzurick@canonical.com>
+Forwarded: https://github.com/opensvc/multipath-tools/pull/72
+Bug-Ubuntu: https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/multipath-tools/+bug/2034471
+Last-Update: 2023-09-13
+---
+This patch header follows DEP-3: http://dep.debian.net/deps/dep3/
+--- a/multipathd/multipathd.service
++++ b/multipathd/multipathd.service
+@@ -5,6 +5,7 @@
+ Wants=systemd-udevd-kernel.socket
+ After=systemd-udevd-kernel.socket
+ After=multipathd.socket systemd-remount-fs.service
++Wants=multipathd.socket
+ Before=initrd-cleanup.service
+ DefaultDependencies=no
+ Conflicts=shutdown.target
diff --git a/debian/patches/series b/debian/patches/series
index 1a0661f..dac4dea 100644
--- a/debian/patches/series
+++ b/debian/patches/series
@@ -5,3 +5,4 @@ enable-find-multipaths.patch
 0009-kpartx-rules-use-Debian-specific-partx-path.patch
 0012-Reproducible-build.patch
 0006-multipathd.service-re-add-ExecStartPre.patch
+lp2034471-multipathd-add-Wants-socket.patch
